perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s available perspective:

- Sara knows she is an SLP who works at a community health center with Shirley Whiteplume, a nurse. They are long-time colleagues and close friends.
- Sara knows they shared care for a mutual patient who died, and she attended his funeral with Shirley.
- At the funeral, Sara observed Shirley looking somber and suspected Shirley was deeply affected. Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and that she saw how much Shirley cared. Sara heard Shirley say it had been tough, that she kept wondering if more could have been done, and that it was hard to let go. Sara said they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought him.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara brought up the patient’s treatment decisions because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. Sara heard Shirley say she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara replied that they made the best decisions with the information they had and that Shirley should not carry it alone. Shirley said she appreciated it but it was hard to accept.
- Later, Sara observed Shirley being reserved and minimally emotional. In a quiet office moment, Sara told Shirley she had noticed she was holding back feelings and that it was okay to be open. Sara heard Shirley say she did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotions does not make her weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Afterward, Sara felt her previous confrontation might have been too harsh. She apologized to Shirley for possibly coming on too strong. Sara heard Shirley say it had been a bit much but she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley’s demeanor had improved and felt hopeful. Sara asked how Shirley was feeling. Sara heard Shirley say she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work, and Shirley agreed to plan something for the weekend.

Sara does not have access to Shirley’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what Shirley said or what Sara observed, nor to any events she did not witness.
